name: Surface and SDF-Based Representations
text:
# Surface and SDF-Based Representations


## Overview
This family replaces the standard volume density $\sigma$ output of canonical [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) with a Signed Distance Function ([SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md)) or occupancy field to represent geometry [S1, unofficial]. By modeling the scene as an implicit surface, these methods achieve sharper geometry extraction and better surface definition than density-based approaches, which often suffer from "fuzzy" boundaries [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves predicting a scalar field $f(\mathbf{x})$ that represents the signed distance to the nearest surface (or occupancy) at position $\mathbf{x}$, rather than volume density [S1, unofficial]. This scalar field is transformed into opacity $\alpha$ or density $\sigma$ for volume rendering integration [S1, unofficial].

**SDF to Opacity/Density Transformation**
The SDF value $s(\mathbf{x})$ is converted into a probability of occupancy or density using a distribution parameterized by a variance or sparsity term $\beta$ [S1, unofficial].

1.  **Laplacian [CDF](#19197-computational-deformation-field-cdf.md) (Standard SDF):** Used in [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md). The opacity $\sigma$ is derived from the Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) of a Laplacian distribution:
    $$
    \sigma = \begin{cases} 
    \frac{1}{2} \exp\left(\frac{s}{\beta}\right) & \text{if } s \le 0 \\
    1 - \frac{1}{2} \exp\left(-\frac{s}{\beta}\right) & \text{if } s > 0 
    \end{cases}
    $$
    where $\beta$ controls the tightness of the [surface representation](#22781-surface-representation.md) [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md).

2.  **Piecewise Exponential ([I2-SDF](#18170-i2-sdf.md)):** Used in [I2-SDF](18170-i2-sdf.md). The density $\sigma$ is defined as:
    $$
    \sigma(\mathbf{x}) = 
    \begin{cases} 
    \frac{1}{\beta}(1 - \exp(d(\mathbf{x})/\beta)) & \text{if } d(\mathbf{x}) < 0 \\
    \frac{1}{2\beta}\exp(-d(\mathbf{x})/2\beta) & \text{if } d(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0 
    \end{cases}
    $$
    where $d(\mathbf{x})$ is the SDF value and $\beta$ is a learnable sparsity parameter [I2-SDF](18170-i2-sdf.md).

**[Inverse CDF Sampling](#973-hierarchical-sampling-inverse-cdf-sampling.md)**
To sample points efficiently near the surface, methods like [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md) use inverse CDF sampling. Random numbers $u_i \in [0, 1]$ are generated and transformed to sample distances $t_i$ using the inverse of the CDF $\Phi^{-1}(u_i)$, concentrating samples near the zero-crossing of the SDF [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md). Stratification is applied by dividing the unit interval into bins [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md).

**Occupancy Fields**
As seen in [Explicit Mesh and Surface Reconstruction](18458-explicit-mesh-and-surface-reconstruction.md), an occupancy field acts as an indicator of surface presence. For solid objects, the occupancy at the $i^{th}$ sample corresponds to an indicator of whether the sample is inside the surface [Explicit Mesh and Surface Reconstruction](18458-explicit-mesh-and-surface-reconstruction.md).

## Subtopics

### [I2-SDF](18170-i2-sdf.md)
I2-SDF is a neural implicit framework for complex indoor scenes that jointly recovers underlying shape, radiance, and material fields from multi-view images [I2-SDF](18170-i2-sdf.md). It distinguishes itself by decomposing the radiance field into spatially-varying material and emission components using surface-based, differentiable Monte Carlo raytracing, enabling physically based scene relighting and editing [I2-SDF](18170-i2-sdf.md). Unlike [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) approaches that treat radiance as a monolithic field, I2-SDF employs a two-stage training scheme and [error-guided adaptive sampling](#17132-error-guided-adaptive-sampling-bubbling.md) to resolve ambiguities and improve reconstruction quality on fine-grained small objects [I2-SDF](18170-i2-sdf.md).

### [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md)
This method renders geometry by outputting a Signed Distance Function (SDF) value $s$ and a variance parameter $\beta$ from a neural network, then transforming $s$ into opacity $\sigma$ using a Laplacian Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md). It builds on [Model Architecture and Encoding](13550-model-architecture-and-encoding.md) by integrating triplane features and SDF-based sampling. Unlike standard NeRF which outputs density directly, this approach enables tight [surface extraction](#29-surface-extraction.md) and inverse CDF sampling for more accurate depth estimation [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md).

### [Explicit Mesh and Surface Reconstruction](18458-explicit-mesh-and-surface-reconstruction.md)
This family encompasses methods that convert implicit [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) (NeRFs) or signed distance fields (SDFs) into explicit polygonal mesh representations or duplex surface structures [Explicit Mesh and Surface Reconstruction](18458-explicit-mesh-and-surface-reconstruction.md). It solves the problem of high computational cost and lack of explicit geometric topology in volumetric NeRFs by replacing dense ray sampling with surface intersections or deformable anchor grids. It differs from sibling methods like [I2-SDF](18170-i2-sdf.md) and [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md) by prioritizing explicit [mesh extraction](#14720-mesh-extraction.md) or duplex surface approximation for real-time rendering, rather than optimizing a continuous SDF field for volume rendering integration [Explicit Mesh and Surface Reconstruction](18458-explicit-mesh-and-surface-reconstruction.md).

### [NeuralUDF](20281-neuraludf.md)
[NeuralUDF](#20281-neuraludf.md) is a method for multi-view surface reconstruction that uses Unsigned Distance Fields (UDF) and volume rendering to recover surfaces with arbitrary topologies, including open surfaces, without requiring 3D ground truth shapes [NeuralUDF](20281-neuraludf.md). Unlike SDF-based methods that are limited to closed shapes, NeuralUDF avoids the sign ambiguity of SDFs by modeling the distance to the nearest surface as a strictly positive value, using probabilistic models to locate surface intersections and enforce color consistency [NeuralUDF](20281-neuraludf.md).

### [IDR (Implicit Differentiable Renderer)](20341-idr-implicit-differentiable-renderer.md)
[IDR](#20341-idr-implicit-differentiable-renderer.md) is a method for learning a [neural Signed Distance Function](#21608-neural-signed-distance-function-neural-sdf.md) (SDF) and camera parameters simultaneously from uncalibrated images [IDR (Implicit Differentiable Renderer)](20341-idr-implicit-differentiable-renderer.md). It disentangles geometry and appearance by combining a DVR-like implicit surface MLP with a NeRF-like view-dependent branch [IDR (Implicit Differentiable Renderer)](20341-idr-implicit-differentiable-renderer.md). Unlike standard NeRF which models volume density, IDR represents geometry as the zero-level set of an MLP and uses a [neural renderer](#11612-point-based-neural-renderer-architecture.md) to approximate light reflection [IDR (Implicit Differentiable Renderer)](20341-idr-implicit-differentiable-renderer.md).

### SDF-based NeRF
- [S1, unofficial] Uses an SDF representation instead of volume densities to reconstruct scenes from RGB-D data, converting sdf values to densities for the NeRF formulation.

### NeuS (Neural Implicit Surface)
- [S2] A scene representation using two neural implicit functions encoded by MLPs to model accurate surface geometry and appearance from unconstrained Internet photos with varying lighting.
- [S2] $d = \text{MLP}_{\text{SDF}}(\mathbf{x})$, where $\mathbf{x}$ is a point in $\mathbb{R}^3$. $d$ approximates the signed distance to the true surface $S$.

## Background
Azinovic et al. [AMBG∗ 21] propose to use an SDF representation instead of volume densities to reconstruct scenes from RGB-D data [S1, unofficial]. NeuS [WLL∗ 21] ties the volume density to an SDF and reparameterizes the transmittance function such that it achieves its maximal slope precisely at the zero-crossing of this SDF, allowing an unbiased estimate of the corresponding surface [S1, unofficial]. VolSDF [YGKL21b] uses an alternate mapping from SDF to volume density, which allows them to devise a new resampling strategy to achieve provably bounded error on the approximated opacity in the volume rendering quadrature equation [S1, unofficial].
